put.description: Studio takes a checkpoint every everyHours while the sandbox runs, or once after it stopped, or with afterTasks after every agent turn that changed files. It deletes the older ones it took: it keeps the newest three and the newest of each of the seven days before. Checkpoints taken by hand, or renamed, are never deleted. Turning the schedule off keeps the checkpoints it took.

post.description: Captures the disks of a running or stopped sandbox. A running sandbox is frozen while its filesystems are flushed; one created with systemd as its init must be stopped first.

Runs git clone as the agent user in the running sandbox, from the virtual remote https://git.studio.internal/<forge>/<path>.git into /workspace/<repository name>, so the clone fetches and pushes through Studio like any other. A folder of that name that is not empty fails the clone.

get.description: The sandbox's most recent connections, newest first. The log is kept in memory only.

put.description: Gives /workspace, Docker's disk and /home/agent new sizes; a size left out stays. A disk can't change its size in place, so this is a rebase onto the sandbox's own template, or onto the current base image for a sandbox without one, that keeps its CPUs and memory and copies Docker's images, containers and volumes as well as the workspace and the home. A disk may shrink as long as what it holds fits. Software installed outside the three disks, such as apt packages, is lost, and tmux sessions end. A running sandbox is stopped for the copy and started again; a stopped one stays stopped. It returns at once in state creating, with the steps in progress. If the resize fails, the sandbox stays as it was, and its progress names the step that failed until it is dismissed (DELETE …/progress).

post.description: Writes the body as the file name in the folder path (relative to /workspace; empty is /workspace itself). A file is at most 100 MiB and is owned by the agent user, mode 0644. Its name must be one file name. conflict decides a name already taken: fail (the default) answers 409 and writes nothing, replace overwrites a regular file, and keep writes it as "name (2).ext", the next free name. A folder or a link under the name is never replaced. The upload is written under a hidden name and renamed into place, so readers never see half a file.

The files of the sandbox's workspace that a chat message can mention: in a git repository the files git knows, tracked or untracked but not ignored, and the ones it reports changed; elsewhere every file, past the folders of dependencies and caches. At most 20,000 paths.

post.description: Creates a sandbox with the same template and resources and a copy of /workspace and /home/agent, then starts it. It returns at once in state creating; the copy and boot run in the background, and a failed fork stays as a failed sandbox until it is deleted. Docker state is not copied. A running sandbox is copied while it runs, so files written during the copy may be inconsistent.

Studio forks the source into a scratch sandbox <source>-merge-<n> and merges the fork's changes there; the source isn't touched until the merge is accepted. It answers at once in state preparing; the merge becomes ready, conflicts or failed.

post.description: Copies /workspace and /home/agent into a new VM built from the template, with the template's resources, or from the default image with the sandbox's own. Software installed outside /workspace and the home, such as apt packages, is lost. Docker images, containers and volumes are lost. Tmux sessions end. A running sandbox is stopped for the copy and started again; a stopped one stays stopped. It returns at once in state creating, with the steps in progress; the copy runs in the background. If the rebase fails, the sandbox stays on its old template in the state it was in, and its progress names the step that failed until the next rebase or until it is dismissed (DELETE …/progress). With wait=true the answer comes once the rebase has ended.
